findings.title: Unknown Threat Actor Uses AI-Driven ARTEX to Target South Korean Finance
findings.summary_md: CrowdStrike Intelligence disclosed a campaign against South Korean financial organizations active from late September to early October 2026 that used the open-source ARTEX framework alongside LLMs and ended in exfiltrated data. Actor-controlled open directories exposed Claude Code session histories, ARTEX configuration files and Chinese-language prompts; CrowdStrike assessed the operator was likely a Chinese speaker and financially motivated with moderate confidence and did not attribute it to a named group. The ARTEX host used DeepSeek v4.1-flash, with GLM-5.3 and Grok 4.6 also appearing in sessions. This is the earliest dated public disclosure of malicious ARTEX use found for this story.

findings.title: From Penetration Testing to Cyber Threat: Beware of ARTEX
findings.summary_md: CERT-EU warned that it had observed several threat actors using ARTEX, an open-source LLM-driven penetration-testing framework, to automate campaigns and that it had seen similar AI-driven activity against its own constituency that likely involved the tool. The author made the repository unavailable in October 2026 after misuse reports, leaving independent forks rather than an official upstream release. CERT-EU mapped the activity to Active Scanning, Obtain Capabilities: Tool and Exploit Public-Facing Application, and urged isolating internet-facing management panels, emergency patching, MFA, and hunting for automated scanning patterns and ARTEX artifacts.

findings.title: ARTEX: Agentic Asbestos
findings.summary_md: Censys counted 1,465 hosts running an exposed ARTEX console as of 4 November 2026, with about 650 in two identically configured hosting blocks and roughly 815 distinct-looking deployments. It found 155 ARTEX hosts also running at least one other detected threat, including Vshell, Cobalt Strike and Adaptix C2, and 32 open directories on other hosts exposing post-exploitation kits, stagers and implants. Censys also saw open directories on the server named in CrowdStrike's report starting 18 August 2026, seven weeks before that report appeared.

findings.title: Threat Overview of ARTEX Autonomous Penetration Testing Framework, FBI FLASH-20261113-001
findings.summary_md: The FBI FLASH dated 13 November 2026 says malicious actors have used ARTEX since at least August 2026 across finance, government, technology, defense, semiconductor, energy, healthcare, manufacturing, telecommunications and legal sectors. It reports intrusions moving from initial targeting to privileged access in under three hours, a South Korean financial campaign that exfiltrated personal data on about 67,000 people, and a ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply chain compromise with attempted sign-ins to more than 2,250 downstream tenants. Researchers counted over 1,600 publicly exposed ARTEX consoles by early November 2026, and the FBI notes the original repository was pulled on 8 October while forks, archives and a commercial ARTEX PRO build persist.

findings.title: Cyberattack hits the Commission
findings.summary_md: Politico broke the story in Brussels Playbook on 19 November 2026, reporting that the cyberattack potentially compromised swaths of personal data, blocked staff from entering salary and leave information, and prompted the Commission's Corporate Management Board to discuss the crisis. An EU official said most of the attack had been contained but the extent of damage was unclear; CERT-EU had detected earlier that month that international hackers used ARTEX, and the official said some actors misuse such tools and had targeted the Commission. Sysper and MyPMO had been restored earlier that week, though Sysper briefly failed again, and translation services were hit on Tuesday.

findings.title: Gone in three hours: What ARTEX does with your credentials
findings.summary_md: 1Password's 19 November 2026 analysis draws on FBI FLASH-20261113-001 and describes how ARTEX turns exposed credentials into broader access at machine speed. The FBI alert maps 43 ATT&CK techniques, including sub-second checks of Azure SAS tokens, service principals, Kudu credentials and storage account keys, administrator passwords found in JavaScript bundles, forged administrator tokens using unrotated keys, and DCSync against KRBTGT after enumeration of more than 110,000 Active Directory objects. The authors recommend sweeping configurations, pipelines and front-end bundles for secrets, rotating signing and authentication keys, restricting deployment credentials and monitoring privileged role assignments and API traffic spikes.

findings.title: EU Commission hit by large-scale cyberattack with data leakage unknown
findings.summary_md: Euronews reported on 19 November 2026 that the Commission had suffered a major cyberattack with no attribution and no confirmation that staff data was stolen. Quoting spokesperson Thomas Regnier, the article said the attack used a publicly available AI tool and identified it as ARTEX, with detection and confirmation on 22 October and no ransomware request. It noted that HR platforms hold names, pay grades, home addresses and contact details that could feed more targeted campaigns, while internal documents sit on a separate system; Sysper was working again but the Joint Sickness Insurance Scheme remained unavailable.

findings.title: European Commission scrambles to contain AI-assisted cyberattack
findings.summary_md: The Register reported on 19 November 2026 that the attack caused more than 10 days of disruption, taking Sysper and MyPMO offline and affecting translation services; Sysper returned earlier that week but failed again on Wednesday. Citing Politico sources, it said Commission defenders detected ARTEX use and that CERT-EU had warned on 5 November about ARTEX-assisted attacks against organizations under its watch. The article also noted the FBI alert on more than 1,600 exposed ARTEX consoles and cases where attackers reached privileged access in under three hours.
